papers.title_en: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
papers.evidence: 神经与声学嵌入的时间耦合用于注意力解码
papers.tldr: 针对听觉注意力解码中现有模型因数据泄漏、眼动和声学线索等捷径导致泛化差的问题，提出CoupleFlow，通过神经与声学嵌入的时间耦合解码注意力，并利用条件流匹配似然比实现贝叶斯最优决策且校准空测试。在九种EEG/MEG数据集上优于基线，所有空测试保持随机，并推导出证据积累定律，揭示信噪比对解码速度和可靠性的限制。
papers.abstract_en: Auditory attention decoding (AAD) seeks to identify the attended talker from brief noninvasive brain recordings by comparing neural responses with competing speech streams. Recent electroencephalography (EEG) decoders report nearly perfect accuracy from one second of data, yet we show that this performance fails to generalize to unseen speech because models exploit trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues instead of speech evoked neural activity. We introduce CoupleFlow, which decodes attention through temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings. Its predictions remain at chance when the brain signal contains no informative coupling, preventing shortcuts based on speech content or talker identity. A conditional flow matching head implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information between brain and speech. This rule is Bayes optimal when the recording depends only on the attended talker and removes preferences for speech that is likely a priori. We evaluate CoupleFlow with content disjoint splits recovered from the audio and null tests that distinguish genuine temporal coupling from trial recognition. Across nine EEG and magnetoencephalography (MEG) datasets processed through a common pipeline, spanning four languages, high density EEG recordings, listeners with hearing impairment, and a room with multiple talkers, CoupleFlow outperforms linear and deep baselines while all null tests remain at chance. Finally, we derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts accuracy across window lengths from a single parameter per dataset and predicts that parameter from the strength of neural speech tracking. This law identifies recording signal to noise ratio as a limit on decoding speed and reliability and estimates the window length required to reach a target accuracy.

papers.title_en: Controlled Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models: Random Initialisation, Band-Power and Validation-Selected Probes
papers.authors: Mingyu Jeon, Suwan Cho, Jae Young Suh
papers.evidence: 评估EEG基础模型在解码任务中的性能及控制条件
papers.tldr: 本研究针对EEG基础模型评估中缺乏对照的问题，引入随机初始化、频带功率和验证集选层三种控制，对五个公开模型和一个内部模型在多个基准上评估。结果显示，控制条件显著改变结论：测试选层高估性能，随机初始化和频谱基线在睡眠与情绪任务上常与预训练相当或更优，全微调增益有限。作者据此提出四项报告规范并公开数据。
papers.abstract_en: EEG foundation models report downstream gains, yet their protocols seldom include three controls. These are the same encoder untrained, spectral features fitted on the same data, and a layer picked without looking at test scores. We therefore evaluate five publicly released EEG foundation models and an in-house JEPA-style model under one protocol with all three controls and several seeds, on five benchmarks and four added task families. The controls change the reading in three ways. First, picking the probed layer by its test score raises the layer-wise peak by an average of +0.034 and reverses the peak-versus-output gap in 9 of 36 cells. Second, with the layer picked on validation, random initialisation matches or beats pretraining for half of the models on sleep and emotion, and no model beats a five-band log-power baseline on emotion or motor imagery. Third, after full fine-tuning only 5 of 30 pairs gain beyond twice their seed spread, and the one clear loss of -0.290 AUROC persists under matched learning rates. From these results we draw four reporting practices, and we release every cell for re-analysis.

papers.title_en: FOCUS: A Lightweight Mamba-2 Model for EEG-Based Cognitive Workload Classification
papers.authors: Ioannis Kyprakis, Stefanos Gkikas, Chariklia Chatzaki, Zongyi Jiang, Randy Gomez, Raul Fernandez Rojas
papers.evidence: 基于EEG的认知负荷分类，轻量模型
papers.tldr: 在高风险环境中，认知负荷监测需要轻量且准确的生理信号模型。本文提出FOCUS，基于Mamba-2的紧凑模型，使用固定FFT分解五个EEG频带，结合深度可分离卷积和权重共享编码器-瓶颈结构，仅0.04M参数。在11人三项任务的留一被试交叉验证中，FOCUS达到74.75%准确率和0.08ms延迟，实现了性能与计算成本的良好权衡。
papers.abstract_en: Cognitive workload estimation from physiological signals is increasingly relevant in high-risk environments, where continuous and unobtrusive monitoring can inform adaptive systems and safety interventions. This paper presents FOCUS (Frequency-band Optimized Cognitive-load Ultralight SSM), a compact Mamba-2-based model for EEG-based binary workload classification under constrained data conditions. Rather than learning frequency sensitivity from data, FOCUS encodes preprocessed multi-channel EEG using a fixed FFT decomposition that covers the five canonical EEG bands. The proposed model combines depthwise-separable convolution and a weight-shared encoder-bottleneck Mamba-2 pair, with 0.04 million parameters and 0.11 GFLOPs. Evaluated in a pilot study with 11 participants under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation across three cognitively distinct tasks, FOCUS achieves 74.75% accuracy on the full dataset at 0.08 ms GPU model-forward latency. In the weight-sharing ablation, the shared configuration achieves 4.55 percentage points higher accuracy on the full dataset than the non-shared variant while reducing the SSM parameter budget; however, this difference does not reach statistical significance under a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test ($p=0.083$). Overall, the selected FOCUS configuration provides a favorable trade-off between classification performance and computational cost within this controlled pilot setting.

papers.title_en: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
papers.authors: Robert Hogan, Sean R. Mathieson, Aurel Luca, Soraia Ventura, Sean Griffin, Geraldine B. Boylan, John M. O'Toole
papers.evidence: EEG语义分割解码神经活动随时间检测事件
papers.tldr: 针对新生儿脑电图事件检测缺乏通用高效框架的问题，提出基于语义分割的U-NeXt通用检测框架，利用卷积编码器-解码器直接分割通道并保留时间上下文。该框架在低电压间隔、伪影和癫痫等多种事件类型上优于任务特定分类器，并在外部数据集上达到专家级癫痫检测性能，同时推理速度大幅提升，支持实时临床监测。
papers.abstract_en: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.

papers.title_en: One-shot federated unsupervised domain adaptation with Smoothed Knowledge Distillation and teacher refinement
papers.authors: Ali Abedi, Q. M. Jonathan Wu, Ning Zhang, Farhad Pourpanah
papers.evidence: 联邦无监督域适应方法，适用于分散源域
papers.tldr: 针对联邦无监督域适应中多轮通信、复杂聚合和噪声伪标签等问题，本文提出SKD-ETR框架，结合平滑知识蒸馏与EMA教师细化，在单轮通信内利用源模型集成的平滑软伪标签训练学生，并将目标知识反向细化教师，在多个数据集上实现通信与计算高效且鲁棒的域适应。
papers.abstract_en: Federated unsupervised domain adaptation (FUDA) addresses the challenge of adapting models to an unlabeled target domain using decentralized source domains while preserving data privacy. However, existing FUDA methods typically require multiple communication rounds, rely on complex aggregation strategies, and often struggle with noisy pseudo labels and inconsistent source knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose SKD-ETR, a novel one-shot FUDA framework that combines Smoothed Knowledge Distillation (SKD) and Exponential moving average-based Teacher Refinement (ETR). SKD trains a student model on the target domain using smoothed soft pseudo labels generated by the ensemble of source models. This reduces overconfidence, mitigates noise, and improves robustness. ETR further refines each source model by interpolating its parameters toward the student via exponential moving average (EMA), thereby transferring target-domain knowledge back to the teachers. This bidirectional refinement enhances pseudo-label quality and student generalization without additional communication overhead. SKD-ETR eliminates complex aggregation by initializing the student model randomly and performing a single-round distillation process. Extensive experiments on OfficeHome, Office-Caltech, and DomainNet demonstrate that SKD-ETR achieves competitive performance while being communication- and computation-efficient, and robust under noisy supervision. The code for this paper is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/SKD_ETR.
